59:1: He means by His saying, may His praise be exalted, glorify God pray to God and prostrate to Him whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of His creation and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise He says: He is the Exalted in His vengeance upon those of His creation who took vengeance for their disobedience to Him, the Wise in His management of them.
59:2: He, the Most High, means by His saying, It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering, God is the One who expelled those who denied the Prophethood of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, from the People of the Scripture, and they were the Jews of Banu Nadir, from their homes. This was their expulsion from their homes and houses, when they made peace with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, on the condition that he would grant them security regarding their blood, women, and children, and that they would have whatever their camels carried of their wealth, leaving their homes and the rest of their wealth for him. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, agreed to that, so they left their homes, some of them went to Syria, and some of them went to Khaybar. This is what God, the Most High, said, It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering, he said: Al-Nadir until His statement, and to disgrace the wicked. He mentioned all of that about them: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. It was said: Ash-Sham, and they are Banu Nadir, a tribe of Jews, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expelled them from Medina to Khaybar, his return from Uhud. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, From their homes until the first gathering. He said: They are Banu al-Nadir. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought them until he made peace with them regarding exile. He exiled them to Syria on the condition that they would have whatever camels carried except weapons. The weapon is the ring. They were from a tribe that had not been exiled in the past, and God Almighty had decreed exile upon them. If it had not been for that, He would have punished them in this world with killing and captivity. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering, he said: These were the Nadir when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expelled them. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us: Ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, who said: Surah al-Hashr was revealed in its entirety regarding Banu al-Nadir. It mentions what God Almighty afflicted them with of His vengeance, and what He empowered the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with over them and what He did to them. He said, It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering [the verses]. And His saying: For the first gathering, God Almighty says: For the first gathering in this world, and that is their gathering to the land of Ash-Sham. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding his statement, at the first gathering, he said: Their exile was the first gathering in the world to the Levant. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: A fire will come from the east of the earth, and will gather the people to its west. It will spend the night with them where they spent the night, and will take their naps with them where they took their naps, and will consume whoever is left behind. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: It reached me that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expelled Banu Nadir, he said: Go on, for this is the first gathering, and we will follow in its footsteps. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, For the first gathering, he said: Ash-Sham when He returned them to Ash-Sham, and he recited the statement of God Almighty, O you who have been given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming that which is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them on their backs (An-Nisa’: 47). He said: From where their backs came, that is, they returned to Ash-Sham from where they came, they were returned to it. And His statement: You did not think that they would leave means that God Almighty says to the believing companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: You did not think that these people of the Book whom God expelled from their homes would leave their dwellings and homes, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God. Rather, the people thought, as mentioned, that Abdullah bin Ubayy and a group of hypocrites sent to them when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged them, ordering them to remain in their fortresses and promising them victory. Ibn Humayd also told me, saying: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, that a group of Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, including Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Wadi’ah and Malik ibn Nawfal, Suwayd and Da’is, sent to Banu al-Nadir, saying: “Stand firm and resist, for we will not surrender you. If you are fought, we will fight with you, and if you go out, we will go out with you.” So they waited for someone to help them, but they did not do so, and they had fortified themselves in the fortresses of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he descended upon them. And His statement, So God came to them from where they had not expected, God Almighty says: So God’s command came to them from where they had not expected it would come to them. And that command that came to them from God from where they had not expected was that He cast terror into their hearts because of the descent of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among his companions. God Almighty says: And He cast terror into their hearts. And His saying: They destroy their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers means, may His praise be glorified, by His saying they destroy their homes the Banu Nadir of the Jews, and that they destroy their dwellings, and that is because they used to look at the wood in what was mentioned in their homes that they liked, or the column or the door, and they would remove that from it with their own hands and the hands of the believers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, They destroy their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers, they began to destroy them from their interiors, and the believers began to destroy them from their exteriors. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: When they made peace with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would not take a piece of wood that pleased them, and that was its destruction. Qatada said: The Muslims would destroy what was near them on the outside, and the Jews would destroy it on the inside. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, who said: They carried from their wealth, meaning Banu Nadir, what camels could carry. A man among them would demolish his house from the top of its door, and place it on the back of his camel and set off with it. He said: That is what His statement means: They destroy their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. That is their demolishing their houses from the top of their doors when they carried them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God Almighty, They destroy their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers, he said: These are the Banu Nadir, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with them for what the camels carried, but they began to pull out the pegs and destroy their homes. Others said: It was said thus because they were destroying their homes in order to rebuild what the Muslims had destroyed of their fortresses. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “They destroy their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take admonition, you who have vision.” He said: He means Banu Nadir. Whenever the Muslims destroyed one of their fortresses, they would demolish their houses and destroy them, then they would rebuild what the Muslims had destroyed, and that was their destruction. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, They destroy their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers, meaning the people of An-Nadir. Every time the Muslims demolished their fortress, they began to demolish their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers, then they would rebuild what the Muslims had destroyed. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of reciters of the Hijaz, Madinah and Iraq, except for Abu Amr, read it as yakhribun with a soft ra, meaning they destroy it and leave it in ruins. Abu Amr used to read it as yakhribun with a shaddah on the ra, meaning they demolish their homes. It has been mentioned from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Hasan al-Basri that they used to recite this similarly to the recitation of Abu Amr. Abu Amr, according to what has been mentioned from him, claims that he chose the shaddah on the ra because of what I mentioned, that ikhrab is leaving something in ruins without a sukoon, and that Banu al-Nadir did not leave their homes and move from them, but they destroyed them by demolishing and demolishing, and that, in what he said, does not happen except with a shaddah. The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads it with a light pronunciation, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language used to say: Takhreeb and Ikhraab have the same meaning, but that is only in the difference in the wording, not the difference in meaning. And His statement, So take heed, you people of insight, God Almighty says: So take heed, you people of understanding, of what God has brought upon these Jews, into whose hearts He has cast terror while they are in their fortresses, as a form of His vengeance. And know that God is the protector of whoever befriends Him, and the supporter of His Messenger against all who oppose Him, and He has brought upon him a form of His vengeance similar to what He brought upon Banu Nadir. What is meant by sights in this passage is the sight of the hearts, and that is because taking heed with them is not like seeing with the eyes.
59:3: God Almighty says: And had it not been that God had decreed and written in the Mother of the Book the expulsion of these Jews from Banu Nadir, which is moving from one place to another, and from one town to another. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And had God not decreed upon them exile, the people’s departure from one country to another. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And had God not decreed upon them exile. And exile is their expulsion from their land to another land. He said: And exile is also said to mean flight, and it is said from it: The people fled from their homes, and I expelled them. And His statement: He would have punished them in this world, God Almighty says, And had God not decreed upon them exile from their land and homes, He would have punished them in this world by killing and captivity, but He lifted the punishment from them in this world by killing, and made their punishment in this world exile and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire in addition to the humiliation that befell them in this world by being expelled from their land and homes. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: The Nadir tribe was from a tribe that had not been subjected to exile in the past, and God had decreed exile for them, and had it not been for that, He would have punished them in this world with killing and captivity. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman: And had God not decreed exile upon them and had there not been a punishment for them from God He would have punished them in this world meaning with the sword and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire in addition to that. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And had God not decreed upon them exile, He would have punished them in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have the punishment of the Fire. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had besieged them until he had exhausted all their power, so they gave him what he wanted from them, so he made peace with them on the condition that he spare their blood, expel them from their land and homeland, and send them to Adhraat in Syria, and he gave every three of them a camel and a water skin. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And had God not decreed upon them expulsion, the people of An-Nadir, whom the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged until he had exhausted all of them, so they gave the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what he wanted. Then he mentioned something similar, and added to it: This is the expulsion.
59:4: And His statement: That is because they opposed God and His Messenger, God Almighty says: This is what God did to these Jews, which was to expel them from their homes, and cast terror into their hearts from the believers, and make for them in the Hereafter the punishment of Hellfire because of what they did in this world, by opposing God and His Messenger in His commands and prohibitions, and disobeying their Lord in what He commanded them to do in following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And whoever opposes God - then indeed, God is severe in penalty, God Almighty says: And whoever opposes God in His commands and prohibitions - then indeed, God is severe in penalty.
59:5: God Almighty says: Whatever types of palm trees you cut down, or whatever you left standing on their roots. The interpreters differed on the meaning of al-Laynah. Some of them said: It refers to all types of palm trees except for Ajwa. Who said that? Bashar told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah: What you cut down of the palm trees he said: the palm tree. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, that he said regarding this verse, What you cut down of the date palms or left behind, he said: The date palm is the date palm smaller than the Ajwa date. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, regarding his statement, What you cut down of soft dates, he said: Soft dates are the dates that differ from Ajwa dates. He told us about it again and said: From the palm trees. Yaqub told us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sa`id, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, What you cut down of the date palms, he said: All palm trees except for the Ajwa date. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, What you cut down of the date palms, and the date palm is what is not dated from the palm trees. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri: What you cut from the soft dates refers to all types of palm trees except Ajwa. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, What you cut of the soft dates, he said: the palm tree, not the Ajwa. Others said: All palm trees are soft, including Ajwa and non-Ajwa dates. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: What you cut down of the palm trees, he said: the palm tree. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, What you cut down of palm trees, he said: Date palms. He said: Some of the Muhajireen forbade others from cutting down date palms, and they said: They are only spoils of war for the Muslims, and the revelation of the Qur’an confirms the one who forbade cutting them down, and absolves the one who cut them down from sin, and he only cut them down and left them with His permission. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, What you cut down of the palm trees, he said: the palm tree. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, What you cut down of the soft palm trees, he said: The soft palm tree is the palm tree, whether it was Ajwa or other. God said, What you cut down of the soft palm trees, he said: What they cut down of the palm trees of Nadir when Nadir betrayed them. Others said: It is a type of palm tree. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, What you cut down of the soft palm trees, he said: The soft palm tree is a type of palm tree. Others said: They are the most generous palm trees. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, he said: Sufyan told us regarding what you have cut down of the date palms, he said: from their noble palm trees. The correct statement about this is the statement of those who said: The soft one is the palm tree, and they are from the types of palm trees as long as they are not Ajwa, and it is them that Dhu al-Rummah meant when he said: The path of fear is falling on the soft dew of the night, its feathers are trickling Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: Layna is from color, and the singular of layna in the plural is layna. He said: It is called layna because it is a verb from fa’la, which means color, and it is a type of palm tree, but when the letter before it was broken, it changed to a ya’. Some of them used to deny this saying and say: If it were as he said, they would have pluralized it as lawan, not layyan. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: The plural of layna is layn. This verse was revealed, as mentioned, because when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) cut down the palm trees of Banu Nadir and burned them, Banu Nadir said to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): You used to forbid corruption and criticize it, so why do you cut down our palm trees and burn them? So God revealed this verse, informing them that whatever the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) cut down or left, it was done by the command of God. Others said: Rather, this was revealed because of a difference of opinion among Muslims about cutting it off or leaving it. It was mentioned that it was revealed because the Jews said to the Muslims what they said: Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated: Yazid ibn Ruman narrated: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) descended upon them, meaning Banu al-Nadir, they took refuge in the fortresses from him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered the cutting down of the palm trees and their burning. They called out to him, O Muhammad, you used to forbid corruption and criticize those who committed it, so what about cutting down and burning the palm trees? Then God, the Almighty, revealed, Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by God’s permission and in order that He might disgrace the wicked. It was mentioned that it was revealed because of a disagreement among Muslims regarding the matter. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Whatever palm trees you cut down or left behind… the verse, meaning to admonish them. So the Muslims cut down the palm trees on that day, and others held back, fearing that it would be a cause of corruption. So the Jews said, Has God given you permission to commit corruption? So God revealed, Whatever palm trees you cut down. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, he said: Some of the Muhajireen forbade others from cutting down palm trees, and they said: They are only spoils of war for the Muslims, and the Qur’an was revealed confirming those who forbade cutting them down, and absolving those who cut them down from sin, and they only cut them down and left them standing on their roots with His permission. Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Barqi told me, Ibn al-Mubarak said, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut down the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir, and concerning that was revealed the verse: What you cut down of the palm trees… and concerning that Hassan ibn Thabit said: The fire in Bouira was so widespread that it was easy for the leaders of Bani Luay And his saying, By God’s permission, means: By God’s command you were cut off and left, and to anger his enemies with that, and it was not corruption. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman: Then by God’s permission means by God’s command it was cut off, and it was not corruption, but a punishment from God, and to disgrace the wicked. His saying: And to disgrace the wicked means to humiliate those who disobey God Almighty and oppose His commands and prohibitions, and they are the Jews of Banu Nadir.
59:6: The Almighty says: And that which God returned to His Messenger from them, meaning from the wealth of Banu Nadir, it is said from it, the thing returned to someone: if it returned to him, and I returned it to him, if I returned it to him. It has been said: He meant by that the wealth of Qurayzah. You did not mobilize against it any horses or camels meaning: you did not place any horses or camels in it, which are the camels. Rather, the Almighty described that which He returned to His Messenger from them as not being mobilized against it with horses, because the Muslims did not encounter war in that, nor were they burdened with it, but the people were with them, and in their country, there was no mobilization of horses or camels in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And what God bestowed on His Messenger from them - you did not urge upon it any cavalry or camels... the verse, he says: You did not cross a valley to it, nor did you travel to it on foot, but rather they were walls of Banu Nadir that God fed His Messenger. It was mentioned to us, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Any village that gives to God and His Messenger, it is for God and His Messenger, and any village that the Muslims conquer by force, a fifth of it is for God and for His Messenger, and whatever remains is spoils of war for whoever fights over it.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding his statement, And you did not urge against it any cavalry or camels, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with the people of Fadak and villages he named, which I do not remember, while he was besieging another people, so they sent him a peace treaty, and he said, And you did not urge against it any cavalry or camels, meaning: without fighting. al-Zuhri said: So Banu al-Nadir was exclusively for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they did not conquer it by force, but rather by peace, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among the Muhajireen, and he did not give the Ansar anything from it except for two men who were in need. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman: And what God bestowed upon His Messenger from them meaning Banu Nadir you did not urge upon it any cavalry or camels, but God gives power to His messengers over whom He wills, and God is over all things competent. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you did not urge against it any cavalry or camels, he said: Their Lord is mentioning that He gave them victory and sufficed them without a leg or equipment in the case of Qurayzah and Khaybar. What God bestowed upon His Messenger from Qurayzah, He made it for the emigrants of Quraysh. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “And what God bestowed on His Messenger from them - you did not urge upon it any cavalry or camels. But God gives authority to His messengers over whom He wills, and God has power over all things.” He said: God, the Almighty, commanded His Prophet to march against Qurayzah and Nadir, and the Muslims at that time did not have many cavalry or camels. So he made what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had taken he judged as he wished. And there were no cavalry or camels at that time to urge upon. He said: And to urge upon means to put down the cavalry, and it was for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among that were Khaybar, Fadak, and Arab villages. And God commanded His Messenger to prepare Yanbu’, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to it and took possession of it all. Some people said, why did he not divide it? So God, the Almighty, revealed His excuse, and said, What God bestowed on His Messenger from the people of the towns is for God and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the children of Adam. The way. He said: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from.... the verse. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement, So you did not urge upon it any cavalry or camels, meaning the day of Qurayza. And His statement, But God gives His messengers power over whom He wills, I inform you that just as He gave Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, power over Banu Nadir, He, the Most High, is informing you that whatever wealth God bestowed upon him, the Muslims did not fight with horses and riders against the enemies, which they had made peace with him over, was for him alone to do with as he saw fit. He says: So the wealth of Banu Nadir came to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, through peace, not by force, so it is divided. And God is over all things competent, He says: And God is over all things competent, nothing is beyond His power, and by His power to do what He wills, He gave power to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, over the wealth of Banu Nadir that he had power over, so he seized it from them.
59:7: He means by His saying, may He be glorified, what God bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, that God Almighty returned to His Messenger from the money of the polytheists of the towns. Scholars differed about what is meant by this verse in terms of colors. Some of them said: It means the jizya and the kharaj. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah ibn Khalid, on the authority of Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him recited, Zakat is only for the poor and the needy (At-Tawbah 9:60), until he reached, Knowing and Wise (At-Tawbah 9:60). Then he said, This is for them. Then he said, And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger and for near relatives (Al-Anfal 8:41)... the verse. Then he said, This verse is for them. Then he recited, What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns until he reached, for the poor and those who have settled in the home and those who came after them. Then he said, This verse includes all Muslims, so there is no one who does not have a right. Then he said, If I live, the shepherd will come to his donkey while he is walking, and his forehead will not sweat over it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, he said: Muammar told us regarding his statement: What God bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, until it reached me that it was the jizya, and the kharaj: a kharaj from the people of the towns. Others said: What is meant by that is the spoils that Muslims take from their enemy among the people of war by fighting by force. Who said that? Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman: Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, it is for God and for the Messenger - whatever the Muslims fight over with horses and camels, and what was conquered by war by force, “it is for God and for the Messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer - so that it will not be a circulating share among the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from.” He said: This is another division of what was taken by war among the Muslims according to what God has placed it upon. Others said: What is meant by that is the spoils that the Muslims rushed to obtain with horses and riders, and were taken by force. They said that the spoils in the early days of Islam were for those whom God named in these verses, not those who spread rumors about them. Then that was abrogated by the verse in Surat Al-Anfal. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns is for God and for the Messenger and for near relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, he said: The spoils of war were for these, then that was abrogated in Surat al-Anfal, and He said, And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger and for near relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer (al-Anfal 8:41). This abrogated what was before it in Surat al-Anfal, and a fifth was made for whoever had the spoils in Surat al-Hashr. The spoils of war were divided into five fifths, four fifths for whoever fought over it, and the remaining fifth was divided into five fifths, one fifth for God and for the Messenger, one fifth for the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his lifetime, one fifth for the orphans, one fifth for the needy, and one fifth for the wayfarer. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished, Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, allocated these two shares: a share The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his share of his kinship, so they carried it on him in the way of God as charity on behalf of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: What he meant by that was what the people of war had agreed to with the Muslims from their money. They said that his statement, Whatever God has bestowed on His Messenger from the people of the towns is for God and for the Messenger... the verses, is an explanation of the division of money that God mentioned in the verse before this verse, which is his statement, Whatever God has bestowed on His Messenger from them, you did not urge upon it any horses or camels. This is a statement that some of the later jurists used to say. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that the ruling on this verse is different from the ruling on the verse before it. This is because the verse before it is about wealth that God Almighty made for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically and not for anyone else. He did not give anyone a share in it. This is what was reported from Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, sent for me, so I entered upon him. He said: Some households from your people have come and we have ordered a tribute for them, so divide it among them. I said: O Commander of the Faithful, order someone other than me to do that. He said: Take it, O man. While I was like that, his freed slave, Yarfa’, came and said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Zubayr, Uthman, and Sa’d are asking permission. He said: Give them permission. Then he remained for a while, then he came and said: This is Ali and al-Abbas asking permission. He said: Give them permission. When al-Abbas entered, he said: O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this traitorous, wicked man. They came to dispute over what God had bestowed upon His Messenger from the works of Banu al-Nadir. The people said: Judge between them, O Commander of the Faithful, and relieve each of them of his companion, for their dispute has been prolonged. He said: I ask you by God by whose permission the world stands up. The heavens and the earth. Do you know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We do not inherit what we leave behind as charity? They said: He did say that. Then he said to them: Do you know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that? They said: Yes. He said: Then I will tell you about this booty. God has singled out His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with something that He has not given to anyone else. He said: And whatever God has bestowed on His Messenger from them - you did not urge upon it any horses or camels. So this was specifically for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). By God, he did not keep it without you, nor did he keep it for himself without you. He divided it among you until this money remained. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would spend from it on his family for a year, then he put what remained in the money of God. So if this verse before it went on and mentioned the money that God singled out for His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and did not make anything with anyone else, and this verse was report about the money that God made for various categories, it was known from this that the money that He made for various categories of His creation is not the money that He made specifically for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and He did not make any partner for him. His statement: And for the near of kin means: And for the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib. And the orphans are the needy among the Muslim children who do not have money. And the needy are those who are in need and that is the question. And the wayfarer are those who are stranded among the travelers, not for disobedience to God Almighty. We have mentioned the narration that came from the people of interpretation in the previous part of our book. And His statement: So that it would not be a circulating wealth among the rich among you, God Almighty says: And We made what God bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns for these categories, so that that spoils would not be a circulating wealth among the rich among you, one spending it sometimes on his own needs, and another spending it sometimes on the paths of righteousness and ways of goodness, so that they may do that as they wish, but We have established a law concerning it that will not be changed or altered. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of the regions, except for Abu Ja`far al-Qari`, recited it as Kiyala yakun “Dawla” in the accusative case, as I described of the meaning, and that in Yakun there is mention of the spoils, and his saying Dawla is the accusative of the predicate of Yakun. Abu Ja`far al-Fare` recited it as Kiyala yakun in the nominative case, Dawla in the nominative case, and the predicate is his saying: among the rich among you, and with the damma of the dal of Dawla all the reciters of the regions recited it, except that it was reported from Abu Abd al-Rahman that it was opened. The people of knowledge of the Arabic language differed about the meaning of that, if the dal is closed or open, some of the Kufians said: The meaning of that is if the state is opened: and the army will defeat this one, then the defeater will be defeated, so it will be said: The state has returned to these. He said: The state, with the dal raised, is in the kingdom and the years that change and are transformed over time, so that is the state and the states. Some of them said: The difference between the damma and the fatha is that the state is the name of the thing that is traded in particular, and the state is the verb. The reading that I do not permit other than that is Kayla yakun with the letter yaa “Dawla” with the letter dal with the letter d with the damma and the dawla with the accusative in the meaning that I mentioned in that because of the consensus of the proof on it, and the difference between dawla and dawla with the letter dal with the letter d with the damma and the fatha is what I mentioned from the Kufi in that. And His statement, And whatever the Messenger has given you, take it, God Almighty says: And whatever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has given you from what God bestowed upon him from the People of the Qur’an, take it. And whatever he has forbidden you, of misappropriation and other matters, then refrain from it. Some of the people of knowledge used to say something similar to what we say about that, except that he directed the meaning of His statement, And whatever the Messenger has given you, take it, to what he gave you of spoils. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from, he said: He gives them spoils and prevents them from taking spoils of war. His statement: And fear God means: And fear God, and beware of His punishment for your opposition to His Messenger by doing what he forbade you from, and your disobedience to him. Indeed, God is severe in penalty means: God is severe in punishment for whoever He punishes from among the people who disobey His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
59:8: God Almighty says: So that what God has bestowed upon His Messenger may not be a circulating share among the rich among you, but may be for the poor emigrants. It was said that what was meant by the emigrants was the emigrants of Quraysh. Mention who said that. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, What God bestowed upon His Messenger from Quraiza, he made it for the emigrants from Quraish. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr and Sa`id ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, who said: There were some people from the emigrants, one of whom had a house, a wife, a slave, and a camel on which he used to perform Hajj and fight. So God attributed to them that they were poor, and He gave them a share of the zakat. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes… to his statement, Those are the truthful ones. He said: These emigrants left their homes, wealth, families, and clans. They went out for the sake of God and His Messenger, and they chose Islam despite the hardship it entailed, to the point that it was mentioned to us that a man would tie a stone around his stomach to support his back from hunger, and a man would make a hole in the winter, having no other blanket. His statement: Those who were expelled from their homes and their wealth, and his statement: seek bounty from God and His pleasure, the position of seek is in the accusative case, because it is in the position of a state. His statement: and support God and His Messenger, means: and support the religion of God with which He sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. His statement: Those are the truthful, means: those whose description he described of the poor emigrants are the truthful in what they say.
59:9: God Almighty says: And those who were established in the home and in faith meaning: They took Madinah as the city of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and built it as homes, and faith in God and His Messenger before them meaning: before the emigrants, they love those who emigrated to them meaning: they love those who left their homes and moved to them from someone other than them, and by that he meant the Ansar who love the emigrants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And those who were established in the home and in faith before them, he said: The Ansar are a description. Muhammad ibn Amr said: The generosity of their souls. Al-Harith said: The generosity of their souls, based on what was narrated from them about that and their preferring them, and the Ansar did not receive anything from that booty. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And those who were established in the home and in faith before them love those who emigrated to them and find not in their breasts any need for what they were given. He says: From what they gave to their brothers, this tribe of the Ansar, they embraced Islam in their homes, so they built mosques and the mosque, before the arrival of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God praised them well for that, and these two groups first in this verse, took their bounty and went at their leisure, and God confirmed their share of the spoils of war. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God Almighty, And those who were established in the home and in faith before them love, he said: These Ansar love those of the Muhajireen who migrated to them. And His statement: And they find not in their hearts any need for what they have been given, may He be glorified and exalted, says: Nor do those who had settled in the house before them, and they are the Ansar, find in their hearts any need, meaning envy for what they have been given, meaning what the Muhajireen were given of the spoils of war. This is because we mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the wealth of Banu Nadir among the first Muhajireen without the Ansar, except for two men from the Ansar, to whom he gave it because of their poverty. He only did that specifically for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, that he was told that Banu Nadir left the wealth for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Banu Nadir was exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to put wherever he wished. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among the first Muhajirun, excluding the Ansar, except for Sahl ibn Hunayf and Abu Dujana, whom he mentioned as being poor, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave it to them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement, And they find not in their breasts any need for what they have been given, the Muhajirun, he said: Some of the Ansar who spoke about that meaning the wealth of Banu Nadir spoke, so God, the Almighty, rebuked them for that and said: “And what God bestowed on His Messenger from them - you did not urge upon it any horses or camels. But God gives authority to His messengers over whom He wills, and God has power over all things.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Your brothers have left their wealth and children behind and have come out to you. They said: Our wealth is divided among them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is it something else? They said: What is that, O Messenger of God? He said: They are people who do not know how to work, so you should suffice them and share the fruits with them. They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. And similar to what we said about His statement: And they find no need in their hearts for what they have been given, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Sulayman Abu Dawud told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, And they find not in their hearts any need for what they have been given, he said: Envy. He said: Abd al-Samad told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja`, on the authority of al-Hasan a need in their hearts he said: envy in their hearts. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. And His statement: And they give preference over themselves God Almighty says, describing the Ansar who settled in the home and the faith before the Muhajireen, And they give preference over themselves He says: And they give the Muhajireen their money, giving them preference over themselves, even if they were in need He says: Even if they were in need and poverty for what they gave preference over themselves of their money. And poverty is a source, and it is also a noun, and it is everything that you see through like a niche or a gap in a wall, the plural is khisasat and khisas, as the rajaz poet said: He taught the fighters satire And the female observers are from the poor I will show her Dalaj or Mango And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated: Ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be an entertainer, but he did not have anything to entertain him with. He said: Is there no man who will entertain this man, may God have mercy on him? A man from the Ansar called Abu Talhah got up and went with him to his tent. He said to his wife: Honor the guest of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Put the girl to sleep and put out the lamp. I see that you will eat with him, so leave it for the guest of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So she did, and the verse was revealed: And they give preference over themselves, even though they were in privation. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki` narrated to us, on the authority of Fadil, on the authority of Ghazwan, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that a man from the Ansar had a guest spend the night with him, and he had nothing with him except his own food and the food of his children. So he said to his wife: Put the children to sleep, turn off the lamp, and bring whatever you have to the guest. He said: Then this verse was revealed: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul God Almighty says: Whoever God protects from the stinginess of his soul they are the successful those who will remain immortal in Paradise. Stinginess in the speech of the Arabs means miserliness and withholding surplus money. From this is the saying of Amr ibn Kulthum: You see the miserly person if you command him to do so because of his wealth in it, he is humiliated By miserliness, it is said that he is miserly, between miserliness and stinginess, and he is extremely miserly and stingy. As for scholars, they believe that miserliness in this context is eating people’s money unjustly. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Mas’udi told us, on the authority of Ash’at, on the authority of Abu Al-Sha’tha’, on the authority of his father, who said: A man came to Ibn Mas’ud and said: I fear that I may be ruined. He said: What is that? He said: I hear God say: And who is protected from the stinginess of his soul? And I am a stingy man who hardly gives anything out of my hand. He said: That is not the stinginess that God mentioned in the Qur’an. Rather, stinginess is to unjustly consume your brother’s wealth. That is miserliness, and miserliness is an evil thing. Yahya bin Ibrahim told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Jami’, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Hilal, who said: A man came to Abdullah bin Masoud and said: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, I fear that this verse has affected me: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. By God, I am not given anything that I can withhold. He said: That is not stinginess. Rather, stinginess is to consume your brother’s money without right, but that is miserliness. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu al-Hayaj al-Asadi, who said: I was circumambulating the House and I saw a man saying: O God, protect me from the greed of my soul, and he did not say anything more than that. So I said to him, and he said: If I protect myself, I will not steal, I will not commit adultery, and I will not do anything else. And the man was Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. Muhammad bin Ishaq told me, he said: Salman bin Abdul Rahman Al-Dimashqi told us, he said: Ismail bin Ayyash told us, he said: Majma’ bin Jariyah Al-Ansari told us, on the authority of his uncle Yazid bin Jariyah Al-Ansari, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: He is free from stinginess who pays zakat, entertains guests, and gives in times of calamity.” Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam narrated: Ziyad ibn Yunus Abu Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Nafi’ ibn Umar al-Makki, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: If I am saved from three things, I hope to be saved. Abdullah ibn Safwan said: What are they that I will warn you about? He said: I take out a great deal of wealth and spend it in harm’s way, then I say: I am lending this night to my Lord, then my soul returns to it until I return it from where I took it. And if I am saved from the affair of Uthman, Ibn Safwan said: As for Uthman, he was killed on the day he was killed, and you loved his killing and were pleased with it, so you are one of those who killed him. As for you, you are a man whom God has not protected from the stinginess of your soul. He said: You have spoken the truth. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God Almighty, And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, he said: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul and does not take anything from what is forbidden, nor does he come near it, nor does stinginess cause him to withhold anything from what is permissible, then he is among the successful, as God Almighty said. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, he said: Whoever does not take something for something that God Almighty has forbidden him from, and stinginess does not allow him to prevent something from something that God has commanded him to do, then God has protected him from the stinginess of his soul, and he is among the successful.
59:10: God Almighty says: And those who came after those who had settled in the home and faith before the first emigrants, they say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith’ from the Ansar. What is meant by those who came after them, the emigrants, is that they seek forgiveness for their brothers from the Ansar. His saying: And do not put in our hearts any rancor toward those who have believed, means resentment and malice. It was said that what was meant by those who came after them was those who converted to Islam after those who had settled in the home. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And those who came after them, he said: Those who converted to Islam were also described. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Then God mentioned the third group, and said: And those who came after them say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers,’ until he reached Indeed, You are Kind and Merciful. They were only commanded to seek forgiveness for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were not commanded to curse them. He told us that a slave of Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, Hatib will enter the neighborhood of Hell. He said: You have lied, for he witnessed Badr and Hudaybiyyah. He told us that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was harsh with a man from the people of Badr. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “How do you know, Umar? Perhaps he witnessed a scene in which God looked down upon his people and called His angels to witness that I am pleased with these servants of Mine, so let them do what they want.” Some of us continued to shrink from the people of Badr, fearing them. Umar, may God be pleased with him, used to say: And to the people of Badr the perished are destroyed. And this group of the Ansar, may God bestow His praise upon them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And do not put in our hearts any hatred toward those who have believed, he said: Do not make our hearts inherit any hatred toward any of the people of your religion. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais ibn Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, who said: People were of three ranks: the first emigrants, those who followed them in goodness, and those who came after them, saying, “Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.” And the best thing for one to be in this rank. And His saying: For those who believe, ‘Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.’ God Almighty says, informing about what was said by those who came after those who had settled in the home and faith, that they said: Do not put in our hearts any rancor toward any of the people of faith in You, O our Lord. His saying: Indeed, You are Most Kind and Most Merciful means: You are compassionate towards Your creation, and merciful towards those who repent and seek forgiveness for their sins.
59:11: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Have you not looked with the eye of your heart, O Muhammad, and seen those who are hypocrites? And they are, as mentioned by Abdullah bin Abi Salul, Wadiah and Malik bin Nawfal, Suwaid and Da'is, who sent to Banu Nadir when the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, descended upon them for war, saying: Stand firm and resist, for we will not surrender you. If you are fought, we will fight with you, and if you leave, we will leave with you. So they waited for someone to help them, but they did not, and God cast terror into their hearts, so they asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, to expel them and refrain from shedding their blood on the condition that they would have whatever their camels carried of their wealth except the ring. Ibn Hamid told us that. He said: Salamah told us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman. Mujahid said about this: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Have you not seen those who are hypocrites? Abdullah bin Abi Salul and Rafi’ah bin Tabut said, and Al-Harith said Rafi’ah bin Tabut, and he did not doubt him, and Abdullah bin Nabtal, and Aws bin Qayzi. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah, or on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Have you not seen those who are hypocrites? meaning Abdullah ibn Abi Salul and his companions, and whoever among them was like them in their conduct. And His saying: They say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, meaning Banu Nadir. As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, meaning: Banu Nadir. His saying: If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, means: If you are expelled from your homes and dwellings, and are evacuated from them, we will go out with you, so we will be evacuated from our homes and dwellings with you. And His statement: And we will never obey anyone concerning you, meaning: We will never obey anyone who asks us to abandon you and not support you, but we will be with you. And if you are fought, we will surely support you, meaning, even if Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those with him fight you, we will surely support you, the people of Nadir, against them. And His statement: And God bears witness that they are liars means: And God bears witness that these hypocrites who promised Banu Nadir victory over Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are liars in their promise to them of that.
59:12: God Almighty says: If Banu Nadir are expelled from their homes and banished from them, the hypocrites who promised to expel them from their homes will not leave with them. And if Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, fights them, the hypocrites who promised them victory will not aid them. And if the hypocrites aid Banu Nadir, they will turn their backs in defeat from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, fleeing from them. They have abandoned them. Then they will not be aided. He says: Then God will not aid Banu Nadir against Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, but rather He will abandon them.
59:13: God Almighty says to the believers in Him from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: You, O believers, are more feared by the Jews than Banu Nadir from God. He says: They fear them more than they fear God. That is because they are a people who do not understand. God Almighty says: This fear that you have in the hearts of these Jews, which is more feared by them than they fear God, is because they are a people who do not understand the extent of God’s greatness. Therefore, they belittle His sins and do not fear His punishment as much as they fear Him from you.
59:14: And His statement: They will not fight you all together except within fortified villages, God Almighty says: These Jews, Banu Nadir, will not fight you all together except within fortified villages, they will not come out to you in the open, or from behind walls, he says: or from behind partitions. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Medina read it as or from behind walls in the collective sense of walls. Some of the reciters of Mecca and Basra read it as from behind a wall in the singular sense of the wall. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. And His statement: Their violence is severe among themselves, God Almighty says: The enmity of some of these infidel Jews toward one another is severe. You think they are all, meaning the hypocrites and the People of the Book. He says: You think they are united and their word is one. But their hearts are diverse, He says: And their hearts are different due to their enmity toward one another. And His statement: That is because they are a people who do not reason. God Almighty says: This is what I have described to you about the situation of these Jews and hypocrites, and that is the scattering of their desires and their enmity towards one another, because they are a people who do not reason about what is in their good fortune and what is in it for them is loss and deficiency. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “They will not fight you all together except within fortified towns or from behind walls. Their violence among themselves is severe. You would think they were together, but their hearts were diverse. That is because they are a people who do not use reason.” He said: You will find the people of falsehood differing in their testimony, differing in their desires, differing in their actions, and they are united in enmity toward the people of truth. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, You think they are united, but their hearts are diverse, he said: The hypocrites’ religion differs from the religion of Nadir. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, You think they are all one, but their hearts are diverse. He said: They are the hypocrites and the People of the Book. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, something similar. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, You think they are all together, but their hearts are diverse. He said: The polytheists and the People of the Book. He mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading and their hearts are more scattered it means: more scattered, i.e. more different.
59:15: God Almighty says: The example of these Jews from Banu Nadir and the hypocrites in what God will do to them by inflicting His punishment upon them is like those before them meaning: like their likeness. The interpreters differed about who was meant by those before them. Some of them said: What was meant by that was Banu Qaynuqa. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, “Like those who were shortly before them. They tasted the consequences of their deed, and for them is a painful punishment.” He means Banu Qaynuqa. Others said: He meant the polytheists of Quraysh at Badr. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Like those who were shortly before them, they tasted the evil consequences of their deed, he said: The infidels of Quraysh. The most correct of the sayings is to say: God Almighty likened these infidels from the People of the Book to what He will make them taste of His punishment through those who came before them from among the disbelievers of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom He destroyed with His wrath, and the matter of Banu Qaynuqa’ and the Battle of Badr, which were before the expulsion of Banu Nadir, and all of those tasted the consequences of their affair, and God Almighty did not specify some of them in representing these with them over others, and everyone tastes the consequences of his affair, so whoever was close to their time before them, they are represented by them in what they meant by the example. His saying, They tasted the evil consequences of their deed, means that God’s punishment befell them for their disbelief in Him. His statement, And for them is a painful punishment, means: And for them in the Hereafter, in addition to the humiliation they suffered in this world, is a painful punishment, meaning: painful.
59:16: And His statement, “Like Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ But when he disbelieved, he said, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.’” God Almighty says: The example of these hypocrites who promised the Jews from Nadir victory if they were fought, or to go out with them if they were expelled, and the example of Nadir in their deceiving them by breaking their promise and submitting to them when they were in dire need of them and their support for them, is like the example of Satan who deceived a man and promised him, in return for following him and disbelieving in God, victory when he needed it. So he disbelieved in God, followed him, and obeyed him. Then, when he needed his support, he submitted to him and disavowed him, and said to him, Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds, in supporting you. The people of interpretation differed as to whether the person about whom God Almighty said, When He said to man, ‘Disbelieve,’ was a specific person, or was he meant as an example of the person to whom Satan did that? Some of them said: He meant by that a specific person. Who said that? Khallad bin Aslam narrated to us: An-Nadr bin Shumayl narrated to us: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Abdullah bin Nahik say: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: A monk worshipped for sixty years, and the devil wanted to kill him but he exhausted him, so he went to a woman and made her insane, and she had brothers. He said to her brothers: Go to this priest so he can treat her. So they brought her. He said: He treated her, and she was with him. One day while he was with her, he was pleased with her, so he went to her and she became pregnant. So he went to her and killed her. Then her brothers came, and the devil said to the monk: I am your companion, you have exhausted me. I did this to you, so obey me and I will save you from what I did to you. Prostrate to me once. So he prostrated to him, and when he prostrated to him, he said: “Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds.” This is what God says: “The example of Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ But when he disbelieved, he said, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds.’”. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Mas’udi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, regarding this verse: “The example of Satan when he says to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ And when he disbelieves, he says, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.’” He said: There was a woman who was tending sheep, and she had four brothers. She would go at night to the cell of a monk. The monk went down and committed adultery with her, and she became pregnant. Satan came to him and said to him, ‘Kill her and then bury her, for you are a truthful man who listens to your words.’ So he killed her and buried her. Satan came to her brothers in a dream and said to them, ‘The monk, the owner of the cell, committed adultery with your sister, and when she became pregnant, he killed her and then buried her in such-and-such a place. When morning came, one of them said, ‘By God, I saw a vision last night, and I do not know whether to relate it to you or leave it?’” They said: No, but tell us about it. He said: So he told it. The other said: And by God, I also saw that. They said: This is for no reason. So they went and took back their kingdom from that monk. They came to him and brought him down. Then they went with him. Satan met him and said: I am the one who caused you to fall into this and no one can save you from it but me, so prostrate to me once and I will save you from what I caused you to fall into. So he prostrated to him. When they brought him to their king, he disowned him and was seized and killed. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The example of Satan when he says to man, ‘Disbelieve’… to And that is the reward of the wrongdoers. Abdullah bin Abbas said: There was a monk from the Children of Israel who worshipped God and worshipped Him well. He was visited from every land and asked about jurisprudence, and he was a scholar. Three brothers had a beautiful sister, one of the most beautiful people. They wanted to travel and it was too much for them to leave her behind, so they began to plot what to do with her. One of them said, Shall I direct you to someone with whom you should leave her? They said, Who is he? He said: A monk of the Children of Israel. If she dies, he will take care of her, and if she lives, he will protect her until you return to him. So they went to him and said: We want to travel, and we do not find anyone more trustworthy or more protective of what he has been entrusted with than you of what he has been entrusted with. If you see that we should keep our sister with you, she is lost and in great pain. If she dies, take care of her, and if she lives, treat her until we return. He said: I will suffice you, God willing. So they went. So he took care of her and treated her until she was healed, and her beauty returned to her. He looked at her and found her pretending. Satan kept tempting him to have intercourse with her until he had intercourse with her and she became pregnant. Then Satan made him regret it and tempted him to kill her. He said: If you do not kill her, you will be disgraced and your resemblance to the child will be known, so you will have no excuse. So he kept at him until he killed her. When her brothers came, they asked him what he had done. He said: She died, so I buried her. They said: You did well. Then they began to see in a dream, and they were told that the monk had killed her, and that she was under such-and-such a tree. So they went to the tree and found her under it, having been killed. So they went to him and seized him. Then Satan said to him: I made adultery attractive to you, and her killing after adultery, so would you like me to save you? He said: Yes. He said: Will you obey me? He said: Yes. He said: Then prostrate to me once. So he prostrated to him and then he was killed. That is what God said: The example of Satan when he says to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ But when he disbelieves, he says, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you.’ Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: There was a man from the Children of Israel who was a worshipper, and he sometimes treated the insane. There was a beautiful woman, but she became insane, so she was brought to him and left with him. He liked her, so he had intercourse with her and she became pregnant. Then Satan came to him and said: If he finds out about this, she will be disgraced, so kill her and bury her in your house. So he killed her and buried her. Then her family came after that some time to ask him, and he said: She died. They did not accuse him because of his righteousness towards them. Then Satan came to them and said: She did not die, but he had intercourse with her, killed her, and buried her in his house in such-and-such a place. Then her family came and said: We do not accuse you. Tell us where you buried her and who was with you. So they found her where he had buried her, and he was seized and imprisoned. Then Satan came to him and said: If you want me to get you out of what you are in so that you can get out of it, then disbelieve in God. So he obeyed Satan and disbelieved in God. So he was seized and killed, and he was exonerated. Satan was with him at that time. He said: I do not know of this verse except that it was revealed about him: “Like Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ But when he disbelieved, he said, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.’” Others said: Rather, he meant all people by that, and they said: This is only a parable given by Al-Nadir regarding the deception of the hypocrites towards them: Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Like the example of Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve,’ the common people.
59:17: God Almighty says: The consequence of the matter of Satan and the human who obeyed him and disbelieved in God was that they would remain in the Fire forever. And that is the reward of the wrongdoers. He says: That is the reward of the Jews of Nadir and the hypocrites who promised them victory. And every disbeliever in God is wronging himself because of his disbelief in Him, that they will remain in the Fire forever. The Arabists differed about the reason for the accusative of his statement abiding therein. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is accusative as a state, and in the Fire is the predicate. He said: If it were in the speech, the nominative would have been better in abiding. He said: Their saying: If you come twice is not an accusative of anything, rather it is an emphasis on whether you came with it or not, it is the same, except that the Arabs often make it a state if it is in it for emphasis and what is similar to it in other places. He said: Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein.
