Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: In the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud: So the outcome of them was that they were in the Fire, abiding therein, he said: And in that they were in the Fire, abiding therein, there is an accusative. He said: I do not desire the nominative even though it is permissible. If you see the verb between two attributes, one of which returns to the place of the other, you put it in the accusative, so this is from that. He said: And similar to it in speech is your saying: I passed by a man carrying his fang, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: And saffron on her collarbones, eastward, with its pearls and its throat Because the collarbones are the clavicles here, so the adjective returns to the name it was placed on. So if the two adjectives differ, the nominative and accusative cases are good. From that is your saying: Abdullah is in the house, desiring you. Don’t you see that the in that is in the house differs from the fi that is in desire? He said: The proof is that by which the accusative is known from the nominative case, you do not see the other adjective coming before the first. Don’t you see that you say: This is your brother, in his hand is a dirham, holding it? So if you said: This is your brother, holding it, in his hand is a dirham, it would not be permissible. Don’t you see that you say: This is a man standing before Zaid, in his hand is a dirham? So this indicates that the accusative case is not possible if the other is not brought forward, and it indicates the nominative case if the other is easy to bring forward.
59:18: And His saying: O you who have believed, fear God. God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Oneness, fear God by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins. And His statement, And let a soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow, means: Let each one of you look to what deeds he has put forth for the Day of Resurrection, whether they are good deeds that will save him or bad deeds that will destroy him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Fear God and let a soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow, your Lord has continued to bring the Hour near until He made it like tomorrow, and tomorrow is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: What you have sent forth for tomorrow means the Day of Resurrection. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, What you have sent forth for tomorrow, meaning the Day of Resurrection. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, and he read the words of God Almighty, And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow, meaning the Day of Resurrection, good and evil. He said: And yesterday is in this world, and tomorrow is in the Hereafter. And he read, As if it had never prospered yesterday (Yunus 10:24), as if it had never existed in this world. His statement: And fear God means: And fear God by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins. Indeed, God is All-Knowing of what you do means: God is All-Knowing and All-Aware of your deeds, both good and bad. Nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for all of them.
59:19: God Almighty says: And do not be like those who neglected to perform what God has enjoined upon them, so He made them forget themselves. He says: So God made them forget their own portions of good deeds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: They forgot God, so He made them forget themselves. He said: They forgot the right of God, so He made them forget themselves. He said: Their own share. And His saying, Those are the transgressors, God Almighty says: Those who forgot God are the transgressors, meaning those who went beyond obedience to God to disobey Him.
59:20: God Almighty says: The people of Hell and the people of Paradise will not be equal. The people of Paradise are the winners, meaning that they will attain what they sought and wanted, and will be saved from what they were warned against.
59:21: And His statement, If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God. God Almighty says: If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, which was stone, you would have seen it, O Muhammad, humbled. He says: humbled, coming apart from fear of God despite its hardness, out of caution lest it not fulfill the right of God that is required of it in glorifying the Qur’an, and it was sent down upon the son of Adam while he was belittling its right, and turning away from what is in it of lessons and remembrance, as if he had not heard it, as if there was deafness in his ears. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God... to His saying, that they might give thought. He said: He says: If I had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it carrying it, it would have split and become humbled from its weight and from fear of God. So God, the Exalted, the Majestic, commanded the people, when He sent down the Qur’an upon them, to take it with intense fear and humility. He said, Thus does God present examples (al-Ra’d 13:17), for the people that perhaps they might give thought. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God, God excuses the deaf mountain, but He does not excuse the wretched son of Adam. Have you ever seen anyone whose sides have come apart from fear of God? And these examples We present to the people, God the Most High says, and these things We liken to people, and that is His, the Most High, making them aware that the mountains are more reverent towards His right than they are, despite their hardness and solidity. And His saying, Perhaps they will reflect, means: God sets forth examples for them so that they may reflect upon them, repent, and submit to the truth.
59:22: God Almighty says: “O people, He from whose fear the mountain splits, He is the One Whom worship and divinity are due only to Him. He knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and sees what is in them of what is seen and sensed. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” He says: He is the Most Gracious of this world and the Hereafter, Most Merciful to those who believe in Him.
59:23: God Almighty says: He is the One Who is worshipped and none but Him is worthy of worship, the King above whom there is no king, and nothing but beneath Him, the Holy. It is said: He is the Blessed. I have previously explained the meaning of sanctification with evidence, and I have mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differ on it, so there is no need to repeat it. Mention of the one who said: It refers to Al-Mubarak. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The Holy means the Blessed. And his saying “Peace” means: He is the One who saves His creation from His injustice, and it is one of His names. As Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: “Peace” means God is peace. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaidullah told us, meaning Al-Ataki, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, regarding his statement, “Peace,” he said: He is God. I mentioned the narration previously, and explained its meaning with its supporting evidence, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. And his statement, the believer, means by the believer: the one who makes His creation safe from His injustice. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The believer is one who believes in his statement that it is true. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The believer believes in his statement that it is true. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: The believer he said: The one who believes. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, The believer, he said: The believer is the one who believes and is certain. People believed in their Lord, so He called them believers, and the Generous Lord believed in them because of their belief, so He made them believe that He should be called by that name. And his saying the dominant the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation, some of them said: the dominant is the witness. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, the Guardian, he said: the Witness, and he said another time: the Trustworthy. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, the Dominant, he said: the Witness. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, the Dominant, he said: God Almighty sent down a book and bore witness to it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Al-Muhaymin means the witness against him. Others said: Al-Muhaymin: the trustworthy. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Al-Muhaymin is the trustworthy. Others said: Al-Muhaymin means the one who believes. Who said that? Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His statement, The Guardian, said: The one who confirms everything that has happened, and he read, And a Guardian over it (al-Ma’idah 5:48). He said: So the Qur’an confirms what came before it of the books, and God confirms everything that has happened about what has passed of this world, what remains, and what has happened about the Hereafter. The first of these sayings was explained correctly in what came before in Surat Al-Ma’idah with the reasons indicating its correctness, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. His saying, The Mighty means the one who is severe in his revenge on those who take revenge on his enemies. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, the Mighty means in his vengeance when he takes revenge. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The Mighty in His vengeance when He takes revenge. His saying, The Compeller, means: He who reforms the affairs of His creation, directing them toward what is best for them. Qatada used to say: He compels His creation to do whatever He wills of His command. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Al-Jabbar means He compels His creation to do as He wills. And his saying the arrogant it was said that he meant that he was arrogant about all evil. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The arrogant he said: He is arrogant to all evil. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Abu Raja’ told us: A man told me, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd, who said: The greatest name of God is God. Have you not heard Him say: “He is God, other than whom there is no god, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him.” He says: To sanctify God and to exonerate Him from the association of those who associate others with Him.
59:24: God Almighty says: He is the worshipped Creator, there is no deity worthy of worship other than Him, and no creator other than Him, the Maker who created creation, and brought them into existence with His power, the Fashioner who created them however He willed, and however He willed. And His statement, To Him belong the best names, means that God Almighty says: To God belong the best names, and they are these names that God named Himself with, which He mentioned in these two verses. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, meaning: everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him and prostrates to Him willingly or unwillingly. And He is the Exalted in Might, meaning: He is the One who is severe in taking revenge on His enemies. The Wise in His management of His creation and directing them toward what is best for them.
